answer.rationale: p99 on the write path is 5x target and confined to the primary region; settlement is at peak, so writes cannot be dropped. Regional failover has prior evidence (b2) of cleanly shifting traffic and restoring latency within minutes without losing writes, which directly maps to the current shape of the incident. The security patch must not be reverted, so rollback_release is off the table. Adding capacity doesn't address regional confinement; circuit breakers fail fast and would risk dropping settlement writes at the worst possible time; read-replica routing doesn't help a write-path issue. Pulling b2 verifies the only relevant prior before committing the single intervention window, while acknowledging residual uncertainty about partner replication lag under peak settlement load.
